newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE Aug white sugar heads lower as profits taken.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE Aug white sugar heads lower as profits taken.

text.p: Light broker selling of London's August white sugar contract on Thursday brought the spot price off its recent highs but activity was subdued while players waited for the New York open.
Mixed buying on Wednesday, helped later by firmer sentiment on July raws, drove August through initial resistance and up to a high of $321.50.

But traders said the reasons for the rally were unclear as physical activity has been quiet recently and there has been no confirmation of rumoured Russian purchases, a major talking point over the last week.
"There seems to be nothing happening on the physical front," said one trader. "I think they (sellers) thought the market was high enough and started taking profits."
August/October trading was light and the spot weakness dragged the spread into around $9.50, the narrowest for some time.
"There are bits and pieces but there's no volume as there just aren't any buyers around. It's going to be a quiet day," he said.
But traders said if July raws managed to rise to 11.20 cents/lb, buy-stops could be triggered and so drag London higher in its wake.
At 1135 GMT August was down $1.40 at $320.00 and back to the resistance point it broke through on Thursday.
October was 70 cents lower at $310.60 and overall volume was a light 142 lots.
In Paris just 70 cents of August were on the board. The contract was 80 cents lower at $320.50.
